financials_interim.notes: Alliance Finance Company PLC (ALLI) is a licensed finance company (NBFI). This filing presents separate Company and Group columns (Group consolidates a subsidiary with NCI), so both GROUP and COMPANY rows are entered per this session's convention. shares_in_issue = 33,696,000 ordinary shares (per note: 'Stated Capital was Rs.613,980,000/- comprising of 33,696,000 ordinary shares issued'). Cross-checked: Company NAVPS Rs.336 = 11,336,429,432/33,696,000 = 336.42, ties; Group NAVPS Rs.349 (equity attributable to holders only, excl. NCI) = 11,750,548,948/33,696,000 = 348.78, ties. The filing discloses only ANNUALISED basic EPS (Company 41.86, Group 45.70 -- i.e. quarterly profit x4/shares). To stay consistent with every other entry this session (which store the actual quarter's EPS, not an annualised figure), eps_basic here is computed as the ACTUAL quarter EPS = profit attributable to equity holders / shares in issue: Company 352,617,063/33,696,000 = 10.46 (x4 = 41.86, ties disclosed annualised EPS exactly); Group 384,976,450/ 33,696,000 = 11.42 (x4 = 45.68, ties disclosed annualised EPS of 45.70 to within rounding). This is a deliberate departure from the filing's own headline EPS presentation, documented here to avoid confusion with other ALLI disclosures that quote the annualised figure. revenue = 'Total Operating Income' (the filing's own subtotal = Net Interest Income + Fee & Commission Income + Net gain/(loss) from trading + Other operating income, net). operating_profit = 'Operating Profit before Taxes on Financial Services'. finance_costs/finance_income left BLANK -- Interest income and Interest expenses are disclosed as separate gross lines but are netted to an explicit 'Net Interest Income' subtotal before Total Operating Income (same structure as AFSL/CDB/AAF this session), so populating them separately would double count against revenue. tax_expense = 'Provision for income taxation' only; 'Taxes on financial services' is a separate VAT-on-Financial-Services levy sitting between operating_profit and profit_before_tax (the filing also nets in 'Share of profit from associates' between the VATFS line and PBT -- included within profit_before_tax as disclosed, i.e. profit_before_tax = 'Profit before Taxation from Operations'). minority_interest (Group only) = Non-Controlling Interest in equity, 241,898,077. current_assets/current_liabilities/inventory/trade_receivables/trade_payables left blank per NBFI convention -- liquidity-ordered balance sheet, no current/non-current split; 'Loans and advances' / 'Lease rentals receivable & stock out on hire' are the core lending book, not trade receivables. Borrowings classification: 'Due to Banks' (a very large balance -- 42% of total Group assets, funded via 12 relationship banks per the Bankers list, and drawn/repaid via discrete 'Loans Obtained'/'Loans Repayments' cash-flow lines rather than an overdraft) is treated as long_term_borrowings alongside 'Debt Securities Measured at amortised cost' (the listed Green and Social Bond debentures, detailed in the explanatory notes with 5-year-plus tenors) -- no current/non-current maturity split is disclosed on this condensed balance sheet, so this is an approximation consistent with how this session treated LOFC's undifferentiated borrowings line; short_term_borrowings is therefore left blank rather than guessed. 'Due to Depositors' (customer deposits) is deliberately EXCLUDED from borrowings per project convention. 'Lease Liability' (right-of-use lease liabilities, Rs.504.8mn) is also excluded, consistent with this session's treatment of small lease liabilities for other NBFIs. capex = 'Acquisition of property, plant & equipment' + 'Acquisition of Intangible Assets' only (excludes 'Acquisition of right-of-use assets', a separate lease-related cash flow line, to keep the capex definition strictly PP&E + intangibles as used elsewhere this session). Impairment/NPL commentary: Gross NPL ratio ticked up slightly to 5.66% (30-Jun-26) from 5.54% (30-Jun-25), and Net NPL ratio to 2.89% from 2.56%, yet the actual impairment CHARGE for the quarter fell sharply -- Group 'Impairment (charges)/reversal for loans and other losses' of Rs.129.4mn vs Rs.223.4mn a year earlier (-42%) -- the single most important driver behind the relatively modest 12% Group PBT decline despite a 13% fall in Operating Profit before Taxes on Financial Services. Other drivers: Net gain/(loss) from trading fell 74% (Group, Rs.33.2mn to Rs.8.7mn) and Other operating income (net) fell 62% (Rs.130.9mn to Rs.49.4mn), both one-off/investment- related lines rather than core lending income. A contingent tax matter is disclosed but not provided for beyond the settled portion: an additional surcharge tax assessment of LKR 892.64mn (LKR 628.6mn surcharge + LKR 264.02mn interest) for the 2020/21 period is under administrative-review appeal -- noted as a gap since the ultimate liability, if any, is not quantifiable from this filing.

interim_updates.note_text: Alliance Finance's Group profit fell in Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026): Profit Before Tax -12% to Rs.668.2mn (Rs.757.0mn a year ago), PAT -8% to Rs.398.4mn, and profit attributable to shareholders -9% to Rs.385.0mn (quarterly EPS Rs.11.42 vs Rs.12.60; the filing's annualised EPS is Rs.45.70 vs Rs.50.39). Total Operating Income fell 5% to Rs.2,582.9mn even though Interest Income rose 10% to Rs.4,365.3mn, because Interest Expense rose 23% to Rs.2,096.5mn -- Net Interest Income was essentially flat (+1% to Rs.2,268.8mn), i.e. the funding-cost increase absorbed all of the lending-income growth. The bigger drag was non-interest income, which fell about 33% in aggregate: Fee & Commission Income -15% to Rs.256.0mn, Net trading gains -74% to Rs.8.7mn and Other Operating Income -62% to Rs.49.4mn (from Rs.130.9mn). Partly offsetting, Impairment Charges fell 42% to Rs.129.4mn from Rs.223.4mn (a Rs.94mn saving) and Taxes on Financial Services fell 6%, while operating expenses rose 5% to Rs.1,537.1mn (Personnel +9% to Rs.709.8mn; Depreciation & Amortisation +29% to Rs.74.4mn). Operating profit before levies still fell 11% to Rs.916.4mn. The effective tax rate eased to 40.4% (from 42.6%) and share of associate profit doubled to Rs.14.1mn. Segment mix is shifting hard toward Gold Loans and Loans: Gold Loans revenue +41% to Rs.1,056.2mn with segment assets +43% to Rs.24.0bn; Loans revenue +27% to Rs.1,432.5mn with assets +14% to Rs.31.9bn; while the traditional Leasing/Hire Purchase/Consumer Durable segment shrank (revenue -12% to Rs.1,822.4mn, assets -8% to Rs.22.5bn). Asset quality deteriorated slightly: Gross NPL ratio 5.66% (5.54%), Net NPL 2.89% (2.56%). Return on average shareholders' funds (pre-tax) fell to 21.8% from 30.6%, interest cover to 1.41x from 1.58x. On the balance sheet total assets were flat at Rs.97.5bn (+0.4% vs March 2026) with liquidity redeployed (cash +117% to Rs.3.46bn; repo -80%; placements -31%; FVTPL T-bills +108% to Rs.3.84bn); operating cash flow was +Rs.3.50bn vs -Rs.4.99bn a year earlier mainly because loan growth slowed (Rs.2.07bn of net new loans vs Rs.6.69bn) and Rs.4.64bn of fixed deposits/repos matured. Capital is strong: Tier 1 12.09% (min 8.5%), Total CAR 16.44% (min 12.5%). No dividend was paid in the quarter (Rs.310.0mn was paid in Q1 last year). Contingent-liability flag: an additional surcharge tax assessment for 2020/21 of Rs.892.64mn (Rs.628.6mn surcharge + Rs.264.02mn interest) is under administrative-review appeal and not provided; 2018/19 liabilities (Rs.159mn + Rs.31mn penalty) have been provided.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: no predecessor quarter is stored for ALLI (first financial_statements entry). The filing discloses only ANNUALISED EPS; the stored eps_basic (11.42 Group / 10.46 Company) is the actual quarter EPS, and the prior-year comparative used here (12.60 Group) is derived as prior-year attributable profit (Rs.424,460,567) / 33,696,000 shares, which reconciles to the filing's annualised 50.39 (x4 = 50.40). Narrative is on GROUP basis; Company-basis PBT fell 16% to Rs.608.0mn and PAT 13% to Rs.352.6mn.
interim_updates.takeaway: A margin-squeeze quarter, not a credit one: lending income grew 10% but funding costs grew 23%, leaving net interest income flat, and a ~33% collapse in fee, trading and other income pushed profit down 8-12%. A 42% cut in impairment charges cushioned the result, so the underlying earnings power is weaker than the -8% PAT suggests. The book is rotating toward gold loans and loans and away from leasing; the unprovided Rs.893mn surcharge-tax assessment is the main tail risk.

operational_highlights: Group PBT -12% to Rs.668.2mn and PAT -8% to Rs.398.4mn; quarterly EPS Rs.11.42 vs Rs.12.60 (filing's annualised EPS Rs.45.70 vs Rs.50.39)
Net Interest Income flat (+1% to Rs.2,268.8mn): Interest Income +10% to Rs.4,365.3mn was fully absorbed by Interest Expense +23% to Rs.2,096.5mn
Non-interest income down ~33%: Fee & Commission -15% (Rs.256.0mn), trading gains -74% (Rs.8.7mn), Other Operating Income -62% (Rs.49.4mn from Rs.130.9mn)
Impairment charge -42% to Rs.129.4mn (from Rs.223.4mn) provided a Rs.94mn cushion; Gross NPL 5.66% (5.54%), Net NPL 2.89% (2.56%) -- slightly worse
Mix shift: Gold Loans revenue +41% (assets +43% to Rs.24.0bn) and Loans revenue +27% (assets +14% to Rs.31.9bn) while Leasing/HP/Consumer Durable revenue fell 12% and assets 8% (Rs.22.5bn)
Return on avg shareholders' funds (pre-tax) 21.8% vs 30.6%; interest cover 1.41x vs 1.58x; Tier 1 CAR 12.09% and Total CAR 16.44% (min 8.5%/12.5%)
Unprovided 2020/21 surcharge-tax assessment of Rs.892.64mn (Rs.628.6mn + Rs.264.02mn interest) under appeal; no dividend paid this quarter vs Rs.310.0mn a year earlier
key_drivers: Funding-cost squeeze: Interest Expense +23% vs Interest Income +10% left Net Interest Income flat despite a larger balance sheet
Non-interest income collapse (~-33%): other operating income -62%, trading gains -74% and fee income -15% removed about Rs.152mn of income versus last year
Impairment charge cut 42% (Rs.223.4mn to Rs.129.4mn) -- a Rs.94mn favourable swing that masks weaker pre-provision profit (operating profit before levies -11%)
Portfolio rotation to Gold Loans (+41% revenue) and Loans (+27%) away from Leasing/HP/Consumer Durable (-12% revenue), with segment assets for leasing down 8%
